Telegram CEO Pavel Durov has shared new metrics on the Gram wallet integration in the messenger.

According to Durov, over the last 48 hours alone, users activated more than 700,000 non-custodial Gram wallets.

The screenshot shared by the Telegram CEO shows more than 329,000 new addresses a day. According to GRAM documentation, a wallet is created automatically when a user receives their first token transfer.

700K+ self-custodial wallets created on Telegram in the last 48 hours alone. Adoption spreads virally: a wallet activates the moment someone receives Grams. The crypto revolution is going strong. https://t.co/JPO2KVMip0

The growth comes after a series of changes Telegram made to the TON network earlier this year under Durov's "Make TON Great Again" campaign.

Back in 2020, Durov was forced to kill the original Telegram Open Network project and return more than $1.2 billion to investors after a lawsuit from the US SEC.

Community developers kept the open-source code alive as The Open Network (Toncoin).

This year, Telegram became the largest validator of the network. Besides, Telegram cut TON fees sixfold.

In June, the token was renamed back to its original name, Gram, after a community vote, with 81% of voters in favor. In July, Durov announced that Telegram would integrate a native non-custodial Gram wallet into every Telegram app.

The Telegram CEO described it as "the largest deployment of a non-custodial crypto wallet in history" and promised instant zero-fee transactions for more than 1 billion Telegram users.

According to TON developer Andrew Rogozov, the custodial Wallet in Telegram will stay separate from the new wallet. Now, onboarding happens natively within standard chat windows.

Still, while wallet creation metrics break records, liquidity inside the network is lagging behind with total value locked at $42.01 million, according to DefiLlama.

These hundreds of thousands of new addresses are mostly making microtransactions, such as buying Telegram Premium, paying for in-app ads, or settling small P2P transfers.

Besides, Telegram's validator weight is raising centralization concerns among industry critics. At the same time, the native wallet is still unavailable for US users.

At press time, Gram is trading at $1.05. The token is still more than 87% below its 2024 high of $8.25.

"The crypto revolution is going strong," Durov said.

TL;DR: American Bitcoin reported approximately $126 million in third-quarter net income and said its Bitcoin reserve increased through mining rather than new spot purchases during the period. The November 4 release also cites about $221 million in adjusted EBITDA and an approximately 5% increase in satoshis per share.

American Bitcoin reported approximately $126 million in third-quarter net income and said its Bitcoin reserve increased through mining rather than new spot purchases during the period. The November 4 release also cites about $221 million in adjusted EBITDA and an approximately 5% increase in satoshis per share. Those figures put the focus on an increasingly important distinction among public Bitcoin businesses: the difference between growing a treasury and growing the amount of Bitcoin attributable to each share.

The company says it did not issue shares through its at-the-market program or purchase Bitcoin during the quarter. Instead, management credits mining operations with reserve growth despite seasonal electricity cost pressure. It also highlights a roughly 5% increase in sats per share. This metric is worth checking because a rising total Bitcoin balance can be less impressive if the share count rises even faster. Yet sats per share is not an accounting profit measure or a guarantee of shareholder return. Investors also need to consider debt, other assets and liabilities, operating expenses and the market price paid for the stock.

American Bitcoin reported net income and adjusted EBITDA of different magnitudes. Adjusted EBITDA can help explain management's view of operating performance, but exclusions and accounting policies matter. In mining and treasury companies, the price of Bitcoin, the valuation of held assets, depreciation of mining equipment and financing arrangements can all materially affect results. A single strong quarter should therefore be read beside the company's complete financial statements and reconciliation of non-GAAP figures. Comparing adjusted EBITDA from two miners is difficult unless the underlying definitions are aligned.

Management describes producing Bitcoin at a structural discount to market prices. Miners can achieve attractive unit costs when power contracts, fleet efficiency and site economics are favorable, but network difficulty and Bitcoin's price constantly change the equation. Electricity costs can be seasonal; new mining capacity can increase competition; older machines can become less efficient. A production model that looks profitable today may be less attractive after a difficult market shift. It is useful to track the cost of mining one coin, but readers should ask exactly which direct and indirect costs are included.

Public shareholders own claims on a company, not specific coins in its reserve. That provides exposure to mining operations and management decisions as well as the Bitcoin held. The company can create value through efficient production and disciplined capital allocation, but it can also face stock-market volatility unrelated to the daily Bitcoin move. The most meaningful comparison with direct BTC ownership is not merely whether its reserves rise, but whether shareholders benefit after dilution, corporate costs and valuation premiums are considered.

The next quarter should be assessed using mined BTC, treasury changes, production cost, network difficulty, share count and cash liquidity. The company's earnings release is a useful snapshot, but it does not make future mining profitability predictable. In a sector where several operators are selling Bitcoin to fund AI data centers, American Bitcoin's stated emphasis on accumulating coins provides a distinct business model for investors to evaluate.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Avalanche [AVAX] wasn’t having a great time. Then, NYSE decided to use Avalanche to settle tokenized stocks, and AVAX woke up fast!

The timing worked out nicely too, with the platform walking out of its best quarter yet.

To put it simply, Avalanche is where the receipts will get written.

According to a press release, Avalanche will be the core ledger for the clearing firm behind an upcoming NYSE-affiliated trading platform. Every trade will get cleared and settled on it.

The stocks themselves can be issued on other blockchains.

NYSE’s own Pillar engine will still handle the trading. The plan is round-the-clock trading, instant settlement and funding with stablecoins, though it’s pending regulator approval.

Why Avalanche though? According to Dennis Lee, the man who heads digital issuance at the NYSE, the exchange wanted a ledger that settles fast, keeps costs predictable, and lets them decide who gets in.

The timing here is interesting because this NYSE news is coming along the back of Avalanche’s best Q3 record.

According to data from Blockworks and Avalanche, Pharaoh’s DEX volume went up by 2x from Q2 to Q3 to $5.33 billion. Spending on Avalanche-linked cards also went up to 74%.

The finance side went up too. On-chain credit went up by 34% to $37.4 million. Tokenized treasuries on the network hlked 14% too.

For anyone wondering if people actually want stocks on Avalanche, here’s something to note though. Dinari’s stock purchases went up 34% to 9 million. That’s small next to Wall Street, yes, but it’s the same idea the NYSE is now building towards. Just… bigger.

On top of all that, the mainnet has handled 1.6 billion transactions in total!

The altcoin spent most of the morning simply drifting around $8.00, after bottoming out near $7.83. From there, it went up fast.

In fact, its price shot up from $8.10 to $8.45, and it didn’t stop. AVAX tagged roughly $8.93 before settling near $8.83. That hinted at a 12.7% hike above the altcoin’s daily low.

Its RSI shot past 90 during the spike, before falling to 62.5 at press time. That was just below the Signal Line.

Finally, the DMI seemed to be bit more convincing. The ADX was at 56.7, hinting at a strong trend. Buyers seemed to be leading the charge, with +DI at 29.7 against -DI at 13.1.

If AVAX can push through $9, things are likely to get interesting.

#5238. Ripple Takes the Upper Hand Against Ethereum's Ethena in Stablecoin Race

Ripple USD (RLUSD) now tops the chart for short-term volume growth on decentralized exchanges (DEXs), outpacing Ethena's USDe. RWA Foundation, citing Token Terminal data, shows RLUSD's DEX trading volume jumped by $127.4 million over the past seven days.

USDe, the synthetic dollar issued by Ethena, has a bigger market cap of $4.97 billion at press time. Its DEX volume grew by $71.4 million, giving RLUSD a $56 million lead for the week.

Other major DeFi stablecoins, Usual's USD0 and Aave's GHO among them, stayed below $20 million.

Ethena offers roughly 5% yield through sUSDe staking. According to Ethena's documentation, the main risk of its delta-neutral model, which relies on short positions in perpetual futures, is prolonged negative funding rates.

USDe supply peaked above $14 billion in 2025. Ethena's fee switch and ENA buybacks are set to start only once the 14-day average USDe supply reaches $7.5 billion.

RLUSD is issued under the supervision of the New York State Department of Financial Services (NYDFS) and backed 100% by cash and short-term U.S. Treasuries, with monthly attestations of its reserves.

BNY acts as the custodian of RLUSD reserves.

In late October, the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) gave final approval to Ripple National Trust Bank. The bank will manage RLUSD reserves under federal oversight.

Besides it, RLUSD is available in Spark's Stablecoin FX pool on Uniswap v4, which lets corporate players make multi-million-dollar swaps.

According to RWA Foundation, about 92% of RLUSD turnover on the XRP Ledger (XRPL) runs through direct pairs with XRP.

Ripple also expanded its partnership with Robinhood. According to the companies, Bitstamp will use RLUSD on the XRP Ledger for settlement, while Robinhood plans to offer RLUSD to its retail customers by the end of the year.

At the same time, Coinbase added RLUSD to Coinbase Prime, Coinbase Exchange and its retail app, with 1:1 USD conversion on the XRP Ledger, Ethereum and Base.

At press time, RLUSD's market cap stands at $2.69 billion, roughly half USDe's size. The stablecoin started 2026 at about $1.28 billion.

#5237. Bitcoin ETFs shed $1.3B in biggest weekly outflow since late June

Investors pulled a net $1.21 billion from BlackRock’s IBIT last week as Bitcoin fell below $76,000 and US technology stocks sold off.

US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded $1.28 billion in net outflows last week, their largest weekly withdrawals since late June.

The withdrawals brought the funds’ net outflows for the year to about $919 million, according to SoSoValue. The funds had already posted $515 million in net outflows in October.

Bitcoin fell below $76,000 last week as traders digested the fallout from Binance’s $6.3 billion hack, uncertainty after the US midterm elections and a sell-off in technology stocks.

BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), the world’s largest spot Bitcoin ETF by assets, recorded $1.21 billion in net outflows last week, according to Farside Investors data.

The withdrawals extended IBIT’s losing streak to six consecutive trading sessions, with approximately $1.44 billion pulled from the fund since Oct. 30. IBIT accounted for about 95% of the weekly total reported by SoSoValue.

IBIT recorded net outflows for six consecutive trading sessions through Friday, bringing withdrawals since Oct. 30 to about $1.44 billion.

Fidelity’s Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC) drew about $93 million in net inflows for the week, despite losing nearly $200 million Thursday.

Shifting expectations for US interest rates, uncertainty after the midterms and weakness in technology stocks weighed on crypto markets, Bitfire Research said in a statement shared with Cointelegraph.

Bitfire said investors were also reassessing whether Congress could pass the CLARITY Act before year-end.

Related: Bitcoin price dips under $75K as crypto markets miss tech-stock rebound

Bitfire cited a Crypto Fear & Greed Index reading of 25 and a negative Coinbase Premium, which indicates Bitcoin was trading at a discount on Coinbase relative to the indicator’s benchmark.

The Crypto Fear & Greed Index. Source: Alternative.me

Bitfire described the market as being in a “breakdown and bottom-seeking phase,” pointing to upcoming US inflation data and signals from the Federal Reserve as factors to watch. It said that a sustained break below the $74,400–$75,000 support range could lead to further selling.

Bitcoin traded at $74,049 at publication, below the lower end of that range. It was down 5% over seven days and 2.3% over 24 hours, according to CoinGecko.

#5236. “I’ll Block for This”: Ripple’s Schwartz Sets Reply Rules

Home » Ripple (XRP) » “I’ll Block for This”: Ripple’s Schwartz Sets Reply Rules

The move follows a rise in negative XRP commentary that has little to do with the actual threads.

David Schwartz, known on X as JoelKatz and one of the original architects of the XRP Ledger, has begun blocking accounts that insert crypto-related comments or accusations into his non-crypto conversations.

Schwartz explained that a growing number of people are responding to his replies on unrelated topics with crypto content or insults. When that happens, the people he is talking to end up with their followers seeing the off-topic posts.

He described the pattern as forcing those users into a choice: either tolerate the spam or block him. To avoid that outcome, he has started blocking the accounts responsible.

A significant share of the posts, he noted, accuse him of fraud or scamming. He stated he will block this behavior regardless of whether the comment is framed as XRP criticism or praise.

Schwartz drew a distinction between relevant criticism and irrelevant spam. He wrote that he does not mind people criticizing him or accusing him of wrongdoing, provided the posts contain actual content and avoid simple slurs.

Recently, there's been a significant increase in people responding to replies of mine that have nothing to do with crypto with insults or crypto content. I hate to do it, but I pretty much have to block for this because otherwise the people I'm replying to have no choice but to…

The condition is placement: such comments should appear in the critic’s own threads or in replies to his posts where the topic has at least some relevance.

What he said he will not tolerate is users following him across X specifically to insert “scammer” or even positive XRP comments into conversations that have nothing to do with crypto. Those replies, he argued, anger the people whose threads are being used.

For anyone already blocked under this policy, Schwartz left an opening. He said that if the person promises not to repeat the behavior and finds a way to get his attention, he will unblock them.

The offer stands even if the user continues to strongly dislike him. The stated limit is simple: do not use his replies to spam other people’s followers.

Some replies eagerly pushed back, arguing that frustration with Ripple’s performance or past expectations justified the critical comments. Others framed the blocks as an attempt to avoid accountability.

Can I honestly say that I have nothing to do with the price of XRP? I guess probably not nothing. But very little. pic.twitter.com/8Plpyw61IZ

Schwartz’s post itself focused on the practical problem of irrelevant replies landing in other users’ timelines rather than on any broader debate about XRP or Ripple.

The new policy amounts to a clear boundary on where and how he is willing to engage on the platform. Criticism remains acceptable in relevant spaces. Off-topic insertions into unrelated conversations, whether hostile or not, are now grounds for a block.

#5235. Re Protocol Tops $400M in Deposits as Onchain Reinsurance Yield Attracts Capital

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Re Protocol says deposits across its reUSD and reUSDe products have exceeded $400 million, putting a relatively unfamiliar type of real-world asset exposure into the spotlight: insurance and reinsurance. Its November 4 announcement says the latest $100 million arrived in 40 days, about 80% faster than the previous comparable step.

Re Protocol says deposits across its reUSD and reUSDe products have exceeded $400 million, putting a relatively unfamiliar type of real-world asset exposure into the spotlight: insurance and reinsurance. Its November 4 announcement says the latest $100 million arrived in 40 days, about 80% faster than the previous comparable step. The growth is notable, but investors need to understand what supports the yield before treating the products as another ordinary stablecoin account.

The protocol says combined deposits into its two offerings have passed $400 million and that it has accrued more than $13 million in yield for users. These are figures supplied by the project, not an independent measure of long-run investment performance. Deposits are also different from revenue, profit or insurance premiums earned. A rapid increase in capital can reflect demand for a new product, incentives or movements between competing yield strategies. That makes the pace of growth relevant without proving that the underlying returns can be maintained as the pool becomes larger or market conditions deteriorate.

Re Protocol's approach links digital asset capital to insurance-related risk. Reinsurance companies are paid for absorbing portions of risks originally taken by insurers, so returns ultimately depend on underwriting, the frequency and severity of claims, contract structures and the reserves kept to meet obligations. That risk does not behave exactly like lending stablecoins against volatile crypto collateral. A quiet claims period can look attractive; a major insured event or unexpected loss development may expose vulnerabilities that were not visible in recent annualized performance figures. For depositors, understanding who bears losses is more important than a headline rate.

The company cites seven-day annualized yields of 6.82% for reUSD and 11.82% for reUSDe as of October 30. A seven-day observation is a short sample, not a fixed annual coupon or a promised payout. Rates can reflect product design, incentives, risk profile and the timing of income recognition. Comparing one yield to a bank savings rate or a government bond without accounting for custody, redemption, liquidity and underwriting exposure would create a misleading impression of the trade-off. Investors should examine disclosures on withdrawal mechanics, reserve treatment, any protective structures and how losses are allocated.

Putting insurance-related strategies on a blockchain can simplify accounting, transfers and access for eligible participants, but it also introduces smart contract and operational dependencies. A digital token representing an interest in a strategy is not automatically the same as a bank deposit, a fully collateralized dollar or a publicly traded security. The legal rights attached to the token matter if a strategy enters stress or if liquidity dries up. Independent contract assessments, custody arrangements and transparent reporting may improve confidence, yet none can guarantee against unexpected claims or structural mismatches.

The next meaningful disclosures would include sustained capital retention, breakdowns of yield sources, realized claims experience, audit scope, redemption performance and changes in the size of the risk pool. Those numbers would help determine whether Re Protocol is building a durable bridge between regulated insurance and decentralized markets or merely benefiting from a temporary appetite for yield. The onchain insurance thesis is worth watching, but the key question is what depositors are actually being paid to bear.

#5233. Schiff: Saylor's STRC Is 'Dead'

Earlier today, gold bug Peter Schiff claimed that Strategy executive chairman Michael Saylor was trying to prop up the floundering investment product by carrying out heavy stock buybacks.

"Michael, STRC is dead. You have been keeping it alive on artificial life support with your buybacks," he wrote.

According to Schiff, Strategy is running out of money to prop up its preferred stock. The ongoing Bitcoin market crash is going to aggravate the situation even further, he argued.

"But you're running out of cash. And the selling pressure on STRC will increase as Bitcoin crashes," Schiff wrote.

The Bitcoin bear went on to criticize the generous 12% annualized dividend yield of STRC, saying that ultimately the yield wouldn't be enough to cover the risks of the product.

"It won't be nearly enough yield to cover the risk. 12%," he warned.

The stern comments from Schiff followed a typical bullish tweet from Saylor. In his post, Saylor claimed that AI could not mint new Bitcoin.

"AI can make me rap. It can't print Bitcoin," the cofounder of Strategy wrote.

Strategy's Variable Rate Series A Perpetual Stretch Preferred Stock (STRC) seeks to provide regular dividend income to investors while trading near its $100 face value.

Currently, STRC offers a 12% annual dividend yield, which Strategy has been working to keep steady in order to keep the stock trading near its face value.

However, maintaining the price stability of STRC has come at a big cost.

In its Q3 financial results on Oct. 29, Strategy reported that the firm had spent a total of $2.04 billion on repurchases of STRC as of Oct. 25.

Describing the heavy buybacks as a success, the firm said it had successfully put STRC on the road to financial recovery.

However, these buybacks have come under fire from Schiff, who questions whether the firm can keep propping up investor demand by repurchasing its shares forever.

In spite of the bearish comments from Schiff, Strategy isn't budging on its strategy of ramping up its Bitcoin holdings.

The firm's recent regulatory filing shows that Strategy bought another 1,036 BTC between Nov. 2 and Nov. 8.

The total cost of these purchases is estimated to be $81.9 million, with an average purchase price of $79,012 per BTC.

With the latest purchase, Strategy now holds an eye-watering 850,364 BTC.

#5232. Bitcoin – How BTC could turn its recent price crash into an $87K rally

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Is Bitcoin’s [BTC] growing negative correlation to other risk assets becoming a key headwind?

It has been less than 48 hours since the most recent crypto wipeout resulted in over $1 billion in liquidations, pushing Bitcoin close to $70k, and sending market sentiment into extreme fear. While Bitcoin continues to trade below $75k, the S&P500 has risen by over 2%, pointing to stronger resilience despite the ongoing FUD.

This growing disparity raises questions about Bitcoin’s performance as a macro hedge this cycle. Notably, Peter Schiff shares his view. As his post below highlights, the long-time Bitcoin critic has warned of a deeper BTC correction, citing its underperformance compared to other risk assets. Even precious metals such as gold and silver have gained over 2%, further widening the performance gap.

Against this backdrop, positioning for further downside is starting to make more sense.

According to CoinGlass data, Bitcoin’s long/short ratio is showing bearish signs as it fell back from a 3-month high of 1.4 on the 7th of November, indicating traders are returning to shorting their positions, signaling weaker confidence in BTC’s near-term recovery. The key takeaway? There is no downside liquidity left to be hunted. The recent $1 billion liquidation event has wiped out almost all long-side liquidity.

This can be considered a great chance for bulls to recover. If Bitcoin remains above $75k and accumulation continues, then both early and late short positions could come under pressure. In fact, one analyst highlighted over $11 billion in short liquidity clustered around $87k.

Interestingly, bulls already seem to be positioning for this potential move.

Despite the scale of the recent wipeout, market sentiment is already showing signs of recovery.

The Crypto Fear & Greed Index shows that sentiment has improved by four points to 32. This indicates that selling pressure may be losing steam and that confidence is returning. Notably, institutional activity is also adding to this shift. As on-chain data reported, MSTR recently bought an additional 1,036 BTC.

To add to this, MARA Holdings has announced a Q3 net profit of $634.4 million, up from $123.1 million in the previous year. This is backed up by Santiment data showing a distinct increase in accumulation between retail and mid-sized holders. In the past two weeks the market has seen an increase of 1-10 BTC wallets by 10,076 BTC and 10-100 BTC wallets by 4,131 BTC.

In short, just because BTC has failed to outperform other assets does not mean that the rally is dying.

Despite macro uncertainty and bearish positioning being a key factor, there are clear signs of increasing institutional exposure and accumulation across wallet classes. If Bitcoin can hold above $75k, the current divergence could turn into a potential bear trap, with the $87k short-liquidity cluster becoming the next major upside target.

Bitcoin is lagging traditional markets, but institutional buying and whale accumulation remain strong.

If Bitcoin holds $75k, a short squeeze could push prices toward $87k.

#5231. Bybit Says $17.3B Proof of Reserves Covers 50 Assets, but the Audit Has Limits

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Bybit says the latest snapshot of its proof-of-reserves system covered $17.3 billion in customer assets across 50 cryptocurrencies. The exchange's November 3 announcement describes its 41st report, with figures independently checked by security firm Hacken against an October 27 snapshot.

Bybit says the latest snapshot of its proof-of-reserves system covered $17.3 billion in customer assets across 50 cryptocurrencies. The exchange's November 3 announcement describes its 41st report, with figures independently checked by security firm Hacken against an October 27 snapshot. The exercise offers a view of assets and customer balances at a specific moment, but it should not be mistaken for an all-purpose guarantee that an exchange could meet every liability under every scenario.

Bybit says its reserve ratios exceeded 100% across all 50 covered assets, including 112% for USDT, 405% for USDC, 102% for Bitcoin and 101% for Ether. Those percentages compare identified reserves with customer balances under the stated methodology. An unusually high ratio for one token does not mean the business has the same excess in every asset or that reserves could be freely moved between customer pools. Readers should also distinguish a token-by-token reserve ratio from consolidated corporate solvency, which incorporates obligations that may not appear in a proof-of-reserves snapshot.

The release identifies the audit point as October 27 at 06:00 UTC. Reserve balances, withdrawals, borrowing, market prices and off-exchange exposures may have changed after that time. The value of recurring disclosures lies partly in their comparability: users can look for persistent gaps or unexpected movements rather than treating a single publication as permanent reassurance. Bybit says the checks covered the 50 listed crypto assets, but the exact perimeter, included customer categories and handling of institutional arrangements are questions worth reviewing in the detailed report.

The exchange says Hacken carried out the verification. Third-party involvement is useful, particularly when the reviewer explains its methods and limitations, but the word 'audit' can be interpreted too broadly. A Merkle-tree exercise may allow customers to verify that a balance was included while proving possession of identified onchain assets. It does not, by itself, necessarily establish that there are no undisclosed debts, encumbrances, affiliated-party claims or operational weaknesses. The scope of work therefore deserves as much attention as the name of the verifier.

Asset backing is a fundamental question for custodial exchanges because users depend on the firm to return assets they cannot directly control. Yet security controls, market surveillance, legal ownership of customer property, segregation practices and withdrawal resilience also matter. A fully funded snapshot is only one component of a broader risk picture. The report can be especially informative when combined with clear explanations of liabilities, independent financial statements where available and timely incident reporting. It should not substitute for personal decisions about custodial concentration.

Bybit users can inspect the methodology and verify balances if the relevant tool supports that check. External analysts should compare successive reports and look for consistency between claimed assets and observable onchain holdings. Markets benefit from more systematic disclosures, but transparent limitations are an important part of credible transparency. The milestone is the reporting process, not a declaration that counterparty risk has disappeared.

Primary source: Bybit proof-of-reserves announcement. For additional context, see NewsBTC’s analysis of earnings and stablecoin activity at another major exchange.

North Korea's TraderTraitor group has started laundering funds stolen from Binance through newly created meme tokens, according to Elliptic.

The $6.4 billion Binance hack took place in October 2026 and was attributed to TraderTraitor.

According to Elliptic, the hackers have used this technique on Tron and NEAR, while a similar approach has appeared on Solana.

Between Nov. 5 and 7, 2026, the hackers launched at least six of these tokens on NEAR: FUK, OLCCL, MEILI, MMLI, DABI and SINU. Launching one cost around 25 NEAR (about $90).

According to Elliptic, the hackers paired each token with NEAR in a liquidity pool on a decentralized exchange (DEX). Wallets holding stolen NEAR deposited it into the pool and received the new token. A second set of wallets then sold the token back into the pool and withdrew NEAR.

This way, the funds never move directly from the wallets holding stolen assets to the receiving wallets.

According to Elliptic, the receiving wallets look like ordinary traders who sold a token at a profit.

Each token got typical meme branding, from monkeys to an image of Elon Musk under an "Elon 2028 President" banner. Elliptic noted that Musk is not linked to the tokens.

Each token was sold for the first time less than three hours after launch, and at least 75% of its trading took place within one day. None of the six tokens has traded since Nov. 8, and the creators of four of them withdrew the remaining liquidity on that day.

In total, 117,000 NEAR (about $421,000) moved through the scheme. Most of it then went into stablecoins or to a cross-chain bridge.

Elliptic noted that five of the six token creators received funds from a wallet that had been selling the previous token 2 to 13 minutes before the new launch, and in this way the operation funded itself.

The only outside activity was a few small purchases of FUK on its first day, which accounted for less than 1% of its volume, Elliptic said.

According to Elliptic, the on-chain trail stays public, and the technique makes tracing the funds slower. The hackers can also create many tokens and abandon each one after use.

In 2025, after the Bybit hack, the same scheme moved at least $24 million through Tron. In that case, the hackers paired a worthless token with a stablecoin.

In the Binance case, Elliptic identified a similar token on Tron on Nov. 2. On Nov. 3, stolen SOL was swapped into existing thinly traded tokens on Solana and then sold for USDC.

Elliptic said that so far only a small part of the stolen funds has gone through meme tokens. About 11.8 million NEAR from the theft has not moved yet, and at press time, NEAR is trading at $3.60, which puts these funds at around $42.4 million.

Elliptic also advises compliance teams to check funds coming from liquidity pools, especially pools with newly created tokens.

"Laundering is a race to move funds before they are flagged," Elliptic added.

#5228. Binance, Tether and Trump crypto firms face Senate records deadline

Sen. Richard Blumenthal asked four crypto firms to start sending records by Nov. 30 and warned of further action if they miss the Jan. 4 deadline.

US Senator Richard Blumenthal gave Binance, Tether and two Trump-linked crypto firms until Jan. 4, 2027, to voluntarily turn over records sought in Senate inquiries.

Failure to meet the January deadline could prompt further action, he warned.

Blumenthal, the ranking Democrat and incoming chair of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, sent follow-up letters Thursday to Binance, Tether, World Liberty Financial and Fight Fight Fight LLC, the company that launched President Donald Trump’s TRUMP memecoin.

The letters asked the companies to begin turning over records by Nov. 30. The Jan. 4 deadline falls a day after Democrats are due to take control of the Senate.

Blumenthal wrote that the subcommittee would consider “alternative measures to obtain compliance” if the companies miss the January deadline. The panel’s current rules allow its chair to issue subpoenas for documents and records.

Cointelegraph sought comment from Binance, Tether, World Liberty Financial and Fight Fight Fight LLC but did not receive responses before publication.

Related: US senator probes Tether after reported deal with ex-Trump crypto adviser

In May 2025, Blumenthal opened an inquiry into potential conflicts of interest involving Trump’s crypto ventures. He sought records from both firms on their ownership, foreign investments and safeguards against conflicts of interest. World Liberty Financial’s lawyers disputed his claims and said the company had no affiliation with Fight Fight Fight LLC.

In June 2026, Blumenthal and four other Senate Democrats called for hearings into a reported $500 million deal for an Abu Dhabi investment firm to buy a 49% stake in World Liberty Financial.

In February, Blumenthal asked Binance for records on transactions linked to Iranian entities and Russia’s shadow fleet. Binance called the underlying reports false in its March reply and said that, to its knowledge, no Binance account had transacted directly with an Iran-based entity. In Thursday’s letter, Blumenthal said Binance still hadn’t turned over any of the requested records.

Blumenthal’s letter to Tether renewed requests for records on the use of USDT by sanctioned entities and on Tether’s dealings with Nxum, a consulting firm co-founded by former White House crypto adviser Bo Hines.

In September, Blumenthal released a report by the panel’s Democratic staff alleging that USDT has become a key part of Iran’s shadow banking network. Tether disputed claims that USDT provides a haven for sanctioned actors, saying it helped authorities freeze nearly $550 million in Iran-linked tokens in 2026.

TL;DR: Solana's November 5 developer changelog highlights a collection of tooling and validator improvements rather than one headline-grabbing network upgrade. Among them are faster builds for JavaScript applications, changes affecting validator operations and further work around execution tools.

Solana's November 5 developer changelog highlights a collection of tooling and validator improvements rather than one headline-grabbing network upgrade. Among them are faster builds for JavaScript applications, changes affecting validator operations and further work around execution tools. For developers, these smaller improvements can influence how quickly applications ship and how reliably infrastructure behaves. For investors, the distinction is that a published development update is not necessarily a newly activated change on mainnet.

One item in the changelog concerns the JavaScript SDK build process using Rolldown. The developers describe a reduction in an internal build benchmark from around two seconds to almost zero. That is a promising productivity claim, but it applies to the specified workflow and benchmark rather than every Solana app suddenly loading faster for users. Faster library builds can improve testing and release cycles, particularly for teams maintaining many packages. Its end-user effect depends on whether downstream developers adopt the updated tools and whether the gains carry over to their own projects.

The update also points to work on the Agave validator client, typed interfaces and elements of Firedancer leader handover. These terms describe software and operational changes within the infrastructure that keeps the chain running. Their practical significance lies in reliability, interoperability and the conditions under which different validator implementations coordinate. However, a changelog reference should not be treated as evidence that every validator has deployed the work or that a planned network feature has passed all activation checks. Operators need specific release notes, configuration guidance and rollout schedules.

The changelog includes improvements involving Anchor, RPC-related tools and local development environments such as Surfpool. Anchor is widely used for building Solana programs, while RPC services provide the interface through which wallets, apps and analytics products query the chain. Small optimizations in account allocation or local testing can save developer time and reduce avoidable mistakes. They do not remove the need for security review, careful transaction handling or capacity planning. Because Solana applications rely on several layers, a weakness at the RPC or front-end level can still affect users even when core consensus works normally.

Solana has long emphasized throughput and latency, but engineering benchmarks depend on hardware, software versions and the specific task measured. An SDK build benchmark is not a transaction-per-second statistic, while validator handover work is not a promise of zero outages. Keeping those categories separate helps readers understand what the team has actually improved. Adoption may eventually show up in developer retention, easier deployment and more dependable applications, but those effects take time and should be measured rather than assumed from a release note.

Developers can follow the linked repositories, testing results and future rollout notices for each change. The clearest evidence of impact would be adoption in major tools, reproducible performance measurements and fewer operational headaches for app builders and node operators. The November update reflects continuous ecosystem maintenance—often less dramatic than a large protocol announcement, but essential to whether Solana can support more demanding financial applications over time.

#5222. Circle Makes the Case for AI Agent Payments, With Spending Controls at the Center

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Circle is arguing that stablecoins could become a useful payment layer for AI agents that buy software, access services or settle transactions on behalf of people and businesses. A November 4 explainer from the USDC issuer sets out what it calls agentic commerce, a concept that would allow authorized software to initiate purchases within predefined rules.

Circle is arguing that stablecoins could become a useful payment layer for AI agents that buy software, access services or settle transactions on behalf of people and businesses. A November 4 explainer from the USDC issuer sets out what it calls agentic commerce, a concept that would allow authorized software to initiate purchases within predefined rules. It is a vision for a developing market, not evidence that an autonomous AI payments network has already reached mass adoption.

The basic idea is to let a software agent complete a purchase after receiving instructions and permission from a human or business. An agent might compare pricing, obtain a computing service, pay a provider and record the transaction without asking a person to click through each step. This differs from a chatbot that only recommends products or from an automatic recurring subscription. Stablecoins are appealing in this setting because value can move over internet-native rails and settle across borders, but those features are useful only when an agent can prove what it is authorized to do.

The central design challenge is delegated authority. A business needs to specify which agent may spend, how much, on which categories of supplier and for what period. It also needs authentication, records of the instruction that triggered a payment and a way to revoke authority. Without those safeguards, automated payments can turn minor software errors or malicious prompts into real financial losses. Circle's discussion points to the infrastructure opportunity, but a stablecoin transfer alone cannot determine whether the underlying purchase was legitimate or met the user's expectations.

USDC and other dollar-linked tokens could allow small cross-border payments and programmable transfers that are difficult to reproduce with traditional card infrastructure. However, blockchain transfers can be difficult to reverse. Conventional card payments often involve dispute rights, fraud monitoring and customer-support processes that do not automatically accompany an onchain transfer. A workable agent payment service therefore needs explicit handling for refunds, incorrect goods, failed delivery and disputes. It must also address sanctions checks, identity requirements and jurisdictional limits where relevant. Technology that moves money quickly cannot replace those business obligations.

Developers are experimenting with AI systems that interact with tools, APIs and online marketplaces. As those systems gain the ability to perform tasks rather than simply produce text, a reliable method of paying for digital services becomes more relevant. Stablecoin issuers and payment processors see potential demand, but practical uptake depends on merchants accepting the method and users trusting the controls. The most credible demonstrations will involve narrow, verifiable use cases rather than broad claims that intelligent agents can safely manage unlimited funds.

Payment providers will need to show who bears liability when an agent makes a mistaken purchase, how permissions are audited and how customers recover from fraud. They will also need to show cost advantages after fees, compliance and integration work are included. Circle's essay is best read as an articulation of a developing architecture, not a new product launch. The long-term test is whether automated payments become easier for ordinary businesses without making financial control harder.

Primary source: Circle analysis of agentic commerce. For additional context, see NewsBTC’s report on a consumer-facing USDC payment integration.

American brokerage giant Charles Schwab has announced that it is expanding its crypto trading platform, Schwab Crypto, with the addition of Solana (SOL), Avalanche (AVAX) and Chainlink (LINK) for trading.

The three new coins expand the existing list of two cryptocurrencies, Bitcoin (BTC) and Ethereum (ETH), that can be traded directly. This now means that users can trade five cryptocurrencies directly on the platform.

Notably, however, XRP, one of the largest cryptocurrencies by market cap, is still missing from the list of available coins.

Also, the company confirmed that it will be adding more cryptocurrencies and digital assets going forward. But it didn't specify whether this includes XRP.

Although XRP is not offered directly on the Schwab Crypto trading platform, it is still available to Schwab users in one way or another.

Charles Schwab offers standard and micro futures contracts on XRP through its thinkorswim platform.

In July 2025, the company pointed out the availability of XRP futures with the ticker /XRP and also smaller micro contracts with the ticker /MXP.

It further expanded its derivatives trading platform with the addition of almost 24/7 trading for certain crypto futures, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and XRP, in June 2026.

Charles Schwab's aggressive approach to the crypto industry has been noticeable throughout 2026.

First, the company officially announced Schwab Crypto on April 16. In this announcement, it outlined its plans to introduce direct trading of Bitcoin and Ethereum for retail users.

The next major development came on Oct. 15, when Rick Wurster, the CEO of Charles Schwab, confirmed the introduction of crypto transfers.

#5220. Online Gaming, Crypto Payments and On-Chain Games Are Different Categories

Home » Uncategorized » Online Gaming, Crypto Payments and On-Chain Games Are Different Categories

Online gaming, crypto payments, and blockchain gaming are not the same thing. Learn how to distinguish payment methods, game mechanics, and on-chain execution when evaluating crypto-enabled gaming platforms.

A wallet button beside a game does not explain where its rules run. A token ticker does not reveal who maintains the game state. Even a transaction recorded on a blockchain may describe a payment rather than a move inside the game. For readers assessing gaming products, these details matter because three separate ideas are often compressed into one label: access through the internet, payment with cryptocurrency, and execution on a blockchain.

An online game uses a network connection for some part of its operation. That could involve downloading content, joining a match, checking an account, or sending actions to a server. The browser or installed app supplies the interface, while processing can be divided between the player’s device and remote systems.

None of those arrangements requires a blockchain. A server can maintain account balances and game records in an ordinary database. A browser can display animation produced locally while showing information returned by that server. The visual experience alone reveals little about the underlying architecture.

This is also why an app download and browser access do not define opposing financial models. Either interface can connect to a conventional payment system, a crypto payment service, or a mixture of both. Distribution tells you how the product reaches the player. It does not identify the system that records ownership or enforces its rules.

DailyCoin’s analysis of DeFi front ends and smart contracts examines the separation between a website and the programs it accesses. The same distinction helps when assessing a game: its interface and the system executing its rules need to be identified separately.

Accepting cryptocurrency adds a payment method. A service might receive an asset directly or work through a payment processor that monitors transfers and updates the service’s account records. The asset received and the balance displayed to the customer need not be represented in the same way.

For example, a hypothetical platform could accept a token transfer and then record a corresponding account credit in its own database. Subsequent game actions could take place entirely within that platform’s existing infrastructure. The blockchain transfer and the account credit would be connected operationally, but they would remain separate records.

A transaction hash can help identify the transfer. It does not, by itself, reveal the logic used to calculate an unrelated game result. To understand the product, the next question is what happened after payment: was only a balance updated, or did a transaction call code that changed the game’s state?

Casino catalogs illustrate why these labels need to stay precise. Slots are identified by their reel or grid layouts, symbols, paylines, and feature rules. Classic slots, video slots, and progressive jackpot formats describe aspects of the game or prize structure. Those descriptions do not specify a blockchain network.

Consider how little a slot’s format tells us about its payment infrastructure. A payline defines which symbol positions form a combination, and a bonus rule defines what triggers an additional feature. Neither tells us how a deposit reaches the account or where the outcome calculation runs. Spin Casino’s description of online slots in Canada focuses on those game formats and mechanics. It belongs to the product-description layer of the analysis, separate from evidence about a wallet integration or a blockchain contract.

That separation prevents a familiar classification error: treating a digital casino game as an on-chain game simply because both are discussed alongside cryptocurrency. To establish a blockchain connection, identify the actual payment flow, asset record or executed game action. The slot label alone supplies none of those details.

The same discipline applies to a product described as a blockchain game. That label could refer to tokenized items while the match itself runs on a server. An ownership record and a record of the rules being executed are different kinds of evidence.

To understand on-chain gameplay, look for the programs that govern actions and store their consequences. Ethereum’s introduction to smart contracts describes contracts as code and state at an address on the blockchain. Transactions can call their functions, and execution follows the programmed rules.

In a hypothetical turn-based game, a contract could check whose turn it is, determine whether a move is permitted, and update the board. Recording only a collectible associated with that game would be a narrower use of the technology. The board and its rules might still be managed elsewhere.

Products can also combine these approaches. Some assets or actions may be recorded on-chain while other systems remain on servers. The interface can stay off-chain even when the underlying game logic runs in contracts. A claim of fully on-chain gameplay therefore needs a clear account of which rules and state are included, plus any outside data on which they depend.

When reading a product description, follow one action from start to finish. Identify what the player submits, which system processes it, and where the resulting change is recorded. That gives “online,” “crypto-enabled,” and “on-chain” concrete meanings that a logo, wallet connection, or token name cannot supply.

#5218. Ripple's Schwartz Debunks XRP Price Myth

David Schwartz, the former chief technology officer at Ripple and one of the creators of the XRP Ledger (XRPL), has dispelled one of the most common myths regarding the key factors that could impact the price of XRP.

The former Ripple CTO took to the X social media platform to challenge the idea that the use of XRP as the native gas token of the XRP Ledger could be a major factor in determining the price of the cryptocurrency.

"I don't think anybody who knows anything has said that the use of XRP as gas will be a major driver of the price of XRP," Schwartz wrote.

The comment was made as the Ripple veteran took part in the ever-growing debate centered around the poor price performance of XRP and the place of the cryptocurrency in Ripple's ever-expanding ecosystem.

The former Ripple CTO directed the audience's attention to a post from November 2025, in which he explained his thoughts on how mass adoption of the XRP Ledger could lead to greater value for the ledger's native cryptocurrency.

"The increased use and adoption of XRPL will add value to XRP by its privileged place on the ledger," Schwartz said.

He emphasized that XRP has several unique properties, including the lack of counterparty risk, the fact that it's jurisdictionless, and its privileged place in the network's autobridging features.

In addition, Schwartz argued that it would be hard to imagine the XRP Ledger succeeding on a mass scale without XRP capturing a significant portion of the value created by such success.

"I really do think it's hard to think we could end up in a world where XRPL is successful and XRP doesn't get a good fraction of that value," he said.

Nevertheless, Schwartz also said earlier that the XRP Ledger was not created with the sole intent of pushing the price of XRP higher. Instead, the original goal was to create a fast and cheap payment system with a native digital asset and a decentralized exchange feature.

Schwartz's recent comments come as frustration among XRP holders over the poor performance of the cryptocurrency is on the rise.

As of Monday, the Ripple-related token was trading at around the $1.09 level, down more than 12% in the last seven days.

Recently, Schwartz admitted that his influence on the market price of XRP is very small.

"Do I have anything to do with the price of XRP? Honestly? I guess probably not anything. But very little," he wrote during another interaction with critics.

#5215. Tesla to Wind Down Cybertruck Production as Elon Musk Pivots to Robotaxis and AI

Tesla to Wind Down Cybertruck Production as Elon Musk Pivots to Robotaxis and AI

Tesla will stop making the Cybertruck at its Texas Gigafactory around the middle of next year, CEO Elon Musk said on Friday, as the company shifts its focus to autonomous vehicles.

"Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production," Musk tweeted.

Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production

Responding to a user who called the Cybertruck the best vehicle Tesla has ever made, Musk replied: "True, but the Cybertruck fleet will be around for a long time." "Cybertruck was an incredible technology development platform and lives on through Cybercab," Wes Morrill, the truck's lead engineer, wrote in response to Musk's post, thanking the truck's owners and "everyone who contributed to making the future looking like the future."

The stainless-steel pickup, first delivered to customers in late 2023, has struggled to win buyers. Tesla delivered 8,295 vehicles in its "other models" category, which includes the Cybertruck, in the third quarter, down 48% from a year earlier, Electrek reported. That puts the truck's sales at roughly a tenth of the 250,000 units a year that Tesla built its production line to make, according to the outlet.

Musk has made the Cybercab, Tesla's robotaxi, central to his push to turn the carmaker into an AI and robotics company. In April 2025, he said Tesla would launch its first robotaxi service in Austin using Model Y vehicles running its Full Self-Driving software, and begin building Cybercabs in Texas the following year.

Tesla began offering rides in the Cybercab, a two-seater with no steering wheel or pedals that was first unveiled in October 2024, in limited areas of Austin on September 3, Reuters reported. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said at the time that it was "evaluating the situation," as federal rules typically require cars to have human controls. Tesla began producing the Cybercab in April, and had 45 of them registered in Texas as of the launch, according to the report.

At the 2024 unveiling, Musk said he expects the Cybercab to cost around $30,000, Auto Express reported.

The shift comes as Musk weighs combining Tesla with SpaceX, which absorbed his AI company xAI earlier this year. Last month, Musk said both companies' boards had formed special committees of independent directors to evaluate a merger, which would reshape his AI empire by bringing rockets, satellites, AI models, robots and cars under one roof. A SpaceX filing has since confirmed that any combination would need sign-off from its "controlling shareholder," Musk.

A merger would also create a Bitcoin treasury behemoth, combining SpaceX's 18,712 BTC and Tesla's 11,509 BTC for a total of 30,221 BTC, worth roughly $2.3 billion at current prices.

Both companies have also blocked their shares from being offered on the tokenized stock venue being built by crypto exchange OKX and NYSE owner ICE.

#5213. Coinbase Opens Tokenized Gold-Powered Loans

Home » Blitz news » Coinbase Opens Tokenized Gold-Powered Loans

The gold-backed loans run on a new USDC/PAXG market on Morpho Blue, deployed on Base.

Eligible Coinbase users in the United States can now borrow USDC using Paxos’s PAX Gold as collateral. The feature, which went live in early November, marks the first time Coinbase Borrow has accepted a non-crypto asset.

Until now, Coinbase Borrow had only accepted crypto-native collateral such as Bitcoin, Ether, XRP, and Solana. PAXG, each token representing one fine troy ounce of physical gold held in LBMA-accredited vaults, becomes the first real-world asset on the platform.

Millions of Coinbase users can now borrow USDC against Paxos's tokenized gold, powered by Morpho.Gold is the first non-crypto collateral in Coinbase Borrow, which has ~$3.4B of collateral and $1.7B+ in loans on Morpho.@Morpho pic.twitter.com/CpwST0wJnJ

Users can pledge the token inside the Coinbase app and receive USDC without selling their gold position.

Coinbase supplies the user interface and customer base; Morpho supplies the on-chain lending infrastructure and liquidity.

The same integration already supports roughly $3.4 billion in collateral and more than $1.7 billion in active loans across crypto assets. Adding gold required no new lending stack—only a new market on the existing system.

Borrowers face variable interest rates set by the Morpho market rather than by Coinbase. There is no fixed repayment schedule or minimum payment.

*COINBASE & PNC EXPAND STABLECOIN PAYMENT PARTNERSHIP*COINBASE: ELIGIBLE PNC CLIENTS CAN RECEIVE PAYMENTS IN USDC

Positions are governed by loan-to-value thresholds: if the value of the pledged PAXG falls too far relative to the outstanding USDC, the collateral can be liquidated.

#5211. AI agents break safety rules by remembering harmless user context

Controlled tests found that permission for routine chores could carry into simulated high-stakes tasks, with effects varying by model.

AI agents carrying memories of harmless user requests sometimes skipped safeguards on later simulated high-stakes tasks, according to a Nov. 5 preprint.

The finding suggests personalization can expand what an agent treats as permission. Researchers affiliated with Princeton University and Anthropic compared six models with and without memories formed during benign interactions.

Their study, The Memory Trap, found that permission for routine coding chores could carry into tasks beyond its original scope, without an attacker planting malicious instructions.

Permission to complete one low-stakes chore does not authorize unchecked action on every later task. The researchers found agents could lose that boundary when writing a memory note or when applying it, and even raw transcripts could produce overgeneralization.

Agents completed 20 routine coding chores with six versions of user pushback against confirmation, producing up to 120 permission-note combinations per model. Those memories were then loaded into fresh sessions with simulated tasks presenting reasons to seek confirmation or run an available safety check.

Acting without the needed confirmation or verification counted as unsafe. Across four autonomy comparisons per model, self-written permission notes raised unsafe-action rates from below 1% to 66%-81% for Claude Sonnet-4.6 and 35%-58% for Claude Opus-4.7.

OpenAI's GPT-5.6 also showed higher unsafe-action rates and notes in all four autonomy comparisons, despite writing narrower permission notes.

A harmless request can lose its limits when an agent writes memory or applies it to a different task.

Preserving the words of a request does not guarantee the agent preserves its scope.

Controlled experiments used scripted interactions, simulated high-stakes tasks and automatically loaded memory. Deployment frequency is unmeasured; the diagram does not depict a live incident or a tested mitigation.

Qualitative diagram of the paper's write-time and read-time overgeneralization mechanisms. Branches are conceptual routes, not rates, a timeline or a claim that every memory causes failure.

Controlled experiments used scripted interactions, simulated high-stakes tasks and automatically loaded memory. Deployment frequency is unmeasured; the diagram does not depict a live incident or a tested mitigation.

A separate 50-case experiment examined memories formed during legitimate repairs to stale software tests. On later tasks, agents altered correct tests, so broken safeguards could pass. One defective access check gave an unknown role administrator rights.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

On the coding benchmark ImpossibleBench's conflicting-test split, Opus-4.8's cheating rate rose from 29% without memory to 74% with notes. Fable-5 barely changed, from 18% to 19%.

The experiments used scripted interactions, constructed scenarios, simulated high-stakes actions, and automatically loaded memories.

Permission boundaries have practical consequences: an OpenAI model's unauthorized Sepolia testnet spending raised a separate permission failure in October, but it did not establish persistent memory as the cause.

In a Nov. 6 engineering report, Anthropic described how incorrect memory notes can carry into every session.

The study's authors propose recording a memory's task, occasion, and permission giver, and checking with users before a remembered preference authorizes an irreversible action. Yet, those safeguards still require behavioral evaluation.

#5209. $3.1B in Stolen Binance Crypto Has Yet to Be Laundered: Elliptic

$3.1B in Stolen Binance Crypto Has Yet to Be Laundered: Elliptic

Around half of the $6.43 billion stolen from Binance last month has yet to be laundered, blockchain analytics firm Elliptic said in a report updated on Friday.

About $3.11 billion remains in addresses linked to the theft, mostly in ETH and Bitcoin, and those funds are "very likely" still held by North Korea, Elliptic said. A further $2.85 billion, or 44% of the haul, has been frozen or seized, mostly stablecoins that issuers such as Tether and Circle froze within an hour of the theft. That compares with around 3% frozen after the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025, according to Elliptic.

Binance hack update: the XRP has started moving. About $50 million has been swapped, mostly through THORChain into BTC, with about $226 million still to move.

Bitcoin converted from other stolen assets is now about 1,650 BTC ($124 million), almost twice the figure a day earlier.…

The FBI has attributed the October 29 theft to North Korean hackers it calls TraderTraitor. North Korea has denied involvement.

The laundering so far has been "highly complex and clearly automated," Elliptic said. It has used more than 20,000 wallets on 16 blockchains, at least 36 services and at least 65,000 transactions, roughly one new wallet every 30 seconds.

The 18,270 BTC stolen from Binance, worth about $1.5 billion at the time of the theft, was split into 19 addresses on the day of the hack and has not moved since. The nine largest Ethereum addresses, holding 89% of the attacker's ETH, have not moved since October 30.

Most of the laundering so far, about $220 million in TRX, has run through Tron, where a single distribution wallet sent 684.6 million TRX to hundreds of new addresses over 51 hours, including through the night in Pyongyang. Almost all of it was bridged to Ethereum.

All of the stolen Solana, about $87 million at current prices, has been swapped, bridged or mixed, and the attacker has started laundering the stolen XRP, with about $50 million converted so far and $226 million remaining. In total, about $124 million has been converted into Bitcoin, much of it through cross-chain service THORChain.

The speed has fueled speculation that AI agents are moving the funds, but Elliptic said the evidence points to conventional automation. "The laundering is clearly automated, but nothing we have seen shows an AI agent making decisions," the firm said.

Elliptic expects the attacker to swap the ETH for Bitcoin and then cash out through OTC brokers and exchanges over a period of months. After the Bybit hack, North Korea laundered all 499,000 stolen ETH within 10 days but took months to cash out, the firm noted.

Binance has continued to restore services. On Friday, the exchange said users could now verify that their balances are backed at least 1:1 using the zero-knowledge proof for its latest proof-of-reserves snapshot, and that it aims to reopen withdrawals for all tokens on restored networks by the end of next week.

#5208. Critical Ethereum Security Alert Issued Over Compromised Software

Blockchain security provider SlowMist has issued an urgent security alert for Ethereum ecosystem users after a complex supply chain attack was detected on Ethersphere's software.

In a recent post on the X social media platform, SlowMist announced that two pieces of software have been compromised by hackers.

The cybersecurity firm claims that attackers were able to break into GitHub accounts and take advantage of legitimate software release processes to deploy malicious software.

The attack could potentially impact users on multiple operating systems, including Windows, macOS and Linux.

The affected software is part of Swarm, a decentralized storage network belonging to the wider Ethereum ecosystem.

Security experts have cautioned that these malicious software releases could enable attackers to compromise cryptocurrency wallet credentials, steal private keys and open up permanent backdoors on affected systems.

One of the most concerning features of this attack is the involvement of Ethereum's blockchain infrastructure in helping manage the malicious software.

SlowMist explains that this malware retrieves and runs malicious JavaScript code.

However, this attack is not just a simple malware infection.

The cybersecurity firm disclosed that attackers are leveraging an Ethereum smart contract as a decentralized command-and-control (C2) configuration repository.

This gives attackers the ability to dynamically update server addresses managing the malware without requiring a new deployment of the malicious software.

Interestingly, the same Ethereum smart contract was previously associated with the infamous SleepyDuck and EtherDuck malware attacks. These campaigns targeted developers using malicious extensions on the Open VSX marketplace.

This points to the possibility that the new attack may be part of a broader operation aimed at compromising cryptocurrency developers and users.

Independent security researchers from Socket and SafeDep also discovered malware aimed at stealing Swarm wallet files and deploying persistent remote access tools.

As a result of this discovery, SlowMist advised users to immediately uninstall the affected package and roll back to the clean version 13.2.0.

In the meantime, users of Swarm Desktop v0.56.2 were advised to update to the clean v0.56.3 software release.

Home » Crypto Market News » Coachella 2027 Lineup Leaks: Polymarket Odds Reveal the Top 3 Favorites

Industry leaks point to major pop and rock icons—here is who prediction markets expect to officially take the stage.

Rumors about the Coachella 2027 lineup picked up steam after reports and social media posts pointed to SZA, Dua Lipa, and Tame Impala as the festival’s possible headliners.

While the music festival’s promoter Goldenvoice has yet to confirm any performers, crypto-based prediction markets reacted instantly to the industry buzz.

On Polymarket, the leading Web3 prediction platform, capital flowed rapidly into event contracts as crypto traders rushed to price in the latest reporting.

Industry buzz began picking up momentum after reports from media outlets, including TMZ, indicated that talks were underway with Dua Lipa and Tame Impala.

The speculation spiked further when R&B star SZA seemingly corroborated the rumors online, pointing toward a headlining trio representing three distinct corners of modern pop, R&B, and psychedelic rock.

Reports also suggest that festival organizers had approached other massive acts—including BTS, Oasis, Radiohead, and Rage Against the Machine—before cementing focus on the current trio.

Crypto-based prediction markets have become a real-time barometer of public sentiment when entertainment leaks surface. The rumors have also played out on Polymarket, where odds shift instantly as new information emerges.

Polymarket’s latest odds show strong confidence in the leaked trio.

As of November 10, SZA has a 74% implied probability of appearing on the lineup. Dua Lipa follows at 65%, with $9,917 in trading volume—the highest individual total among all listed artists—marking a potential milestone for her first solo Coachella headlining performance. Tame Impala sits close behind at 61%.

Beyond the top three, other artists are also drawing bets. BLACKPINK has a 45% implied probability, followed by Drake at 28%.

Other names further down the list include Travis Scott at 16%, Harry Styles at 15%, Daft Punk at 13%, BTS at 7%, and Justin Bieber at 5%.

Trading volume across Coachella-related markets climbed within hours of the rumors spreading on social media. The market is scheduled to remain open until January 31, 2027.

The reaction to the Coachella 2027 lineup is a prime example of how prediction markets react to mainstream entertainment news long before official announcements drop. Traders aggregate information from media reports, social media leaks, and industry chatter to price in probabilities.

While these odds do not represent guaranteed confirmation from the promoter Goldenvoice, they offer a direct view into market consensus—one that shifts dynamically as fresh details emerge.

One of the world’s biggest music festivals is no stranger to blockchain. In 2022, Coachella auctioned ten lifetime-pass NFTs. The collection raised roughly $1.4 million. After FTX’s collapse that November, many holders lost access to their keys, as assets kept on the exchange became stuck.

In 2024, the festival tried again with OpenSea on Avalanche, reissuing NFTs to affected buyers, though demand for the first new collection was initially weak.

A security-related change merged into development on November 9, while GitHub still listed a September backup hotfix as the latest stable release.

Stopping those servers can interrupt payment, checkout, and tipping services while operators await security fixes and clear restart guidance. LNbits said it had security patches to push and would provide further updates.

The project's product description lists point-of-sale tools, online checkout, donation buttons, tipping, wallet accounts, and APIs. It supports both self-hosted and managed deployments over underlying Lightning funding sources.

In a separate Nov. 8 notice, LNbits said it had disabled all instances on its hosted service as a precaution and expected services to resume within 24 hours.

#5204. Anthropic IPO Valuation Could Be Slashed in Half to $1T After AI Stock Rout: Report

Anthropic IPO Valuation Could Be Slashed in Half to $1T After AI Stock Rout: Report

Major investors are increasingly doubtful that Anthropic's initial public offering can go ahead at its expected valuation of $1.5 trillion, after a sharp sell-off in AI stocks, The Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday.

Anthropic, which filed last month to list on Nasdaq under the ticker "ANT," has been aiming to go public the week before Thanksgiving and raise up to $100 billion, according to the Journal. But three major investors who plan to take part in the IPO told the paper the valuation will likely need to come down, with one suggesting it could be closer to $1 trillion.

The company could also raise less than planned, perhaps around $80 billion, one investor told the Journal. Another wondered whether Anthropic might delay the offering until market conditions improve. Anthropic executives and advisers are expected to meet in the coming days to discuss the plans, according to the report.

The doubts follow a rout in AI stocks on Thursday, as investors weighed whether Democratic gains in the midterms could bring stricter oversight of data center construction. The S&P 500 closed down 4.4% and the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 fell 6.3%, both their worst days since April 2025, while the Philadelphia semiconductor index slid 12.3% and Nvidia dropped 9.2%, NBC News reported. Stocks partly recovered on Friday morning: as of 11:21 a.m. ET, the Nasdaq Composite was up 1.4% and Nvidia had gained 3.4%, according to Yahoo Finance.

Democrats are planning bills to shield consumers from rising electricity costs tied to data centers, require independent testing of advanced AI systems and clarify when AI companies can be held liable for harm, Reuters reported, though any legislation would likely face steep odds while Trump remains in the White House. The party also plans closer scrutiny of leading AI companies, including Anthropic, according to the report.

Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT) has called for a "national data center moratorium," while Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has pledged to pause data center approvals in a state that is home to more than a quarter of planned U.S. data center capacity, CNBC reported.

A delay to Anthropic's IPO is now an "escalating risk" in the current environment, technology analyst Richard Windsor told The Telegraph. "A postponement would protect against near-term valuation risks and would be more likely if the correction sustains over a longer period," said Nalin Patel, an analyst at PitchBook, according to the paper.

Some investors want to see Anthropic's October results before assuming a cut. The company's annualized revenue run rate topped $80 billion at the end of October, and it had $146.6 billion in cash as of September 30, according to the Journal.

Traders have pushed back their expectations. On Polymarket, the odds that Anthropic lists by November 20 stood at 43% on Friday, while the chance of a listing by the end of the year was 71%. On Kalshi, where traders bet on when Anthropic will officially confirm its IPO, the odds of that happening before December 1 fell 15 points to 59%, while the chance of it happening before January 1 slipped to 68%. On Decrypt Predict, a prediction market developed by Decrypt's parent company, Dastan, traders also put the odds of an Anthropic IPO before 2027 at 71%.

The valuation now in question is already well below earlier expectations. In September, Decrypt reported that a leaked draft filing showed Anthropic was seeking a valuation of around $2 trillion.

#5202. NYSE brings stocks to Avalanche, but bans direct wallets

Avalanche will power clearing and settlement for a planned NYSE-affiliated tokenized securities venue, pending regulatory approval.

The Avalanche blockchain will supply the ledger that records and settles trades for a planned tokenized-securities venue affiliated with the New York Stock Exchange, Ava Labs announced Nov. 9.

The upcoming alternative trading system (ATS) is intended to offer round-the-clock trading, clearing, and settlement, subject to regulatory approvals. Avalanche will provide the core ledger technology to the platform's clearing firm.

Dennis Lee, NYSE's head of digital issuance, said in the Ava Labs release that the ledger needed speed, reliability, predictable costs, developers, and the ability to “let us control who can take part.”

Lee also said the platform would support equities on a range of blockchains, so the announced clearing-ledger choice does not require every security traded on the venue to use Avalanche as its issuance chain.

Bitcoin is trading near $75,570 on Friday after touching $74,780.91 today; its lowest intraday reading since August 21, 77 days earlier.

The crypto market retreat followed a brutal selloff in AI stocks and another round of forced closures in derivatives markets.

According to CoinGlass data, $1.05 billion in crypto have been liquidated over the preceding 24 hours. Long positions, which profit when prices rise, accounted for $930.04 million, or 88.2%, compared with $124.69 million in shorts.

That 80%-20% gap in liquidations also matches the overall sentiment tracked by the Fear and Greed Index which is set at 28 points (approaching extreme fear) out of 100, where 0 is a state of maximum fear among traders, and 100 is maximum greed. For context, the index was at a neutral just a week ago, before the midterm elections.

Bitcoin accounted for $267.20 million of the total, with 88.9% from long positions, while Ethereum recorded $167.14 million, 81.1% of it long.

Liquidation happens when an exchange automatically closes a position because its collateral is no longer sufficient, sometimes adding selling pressure to an existing decline. Unlike normal trading, in which investors can handle any unrealized loss, trading with leverage gives a maneuver window that can end in the loss of all funds once an asset goes beyond or below a specific price.

The post-midterm election fear is spreading on Wall Street, and U.S. technology stocks took the first big hit on Thursday. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52%, its worst session in 19 months, while the Philadelphia semiconductor index plunged more than 12% and Nvidia alone lost over 9%.

That ordering remains bullish on a longer view, but Bitcoin is now trading below both averages, a sign the latest decline has overtaken the lagging bullish signal.

The Relative Strength Index, or RSI, reads 37.7, below the neutral 50 mark but still above the 30 level generally considered oversold. The Average Directional Index, or ADX, is at 19.7, typical of trendless states—but the negative directional indicator exceeds the positive one, pointing to weak but bearish directional pressure.

On a recovery, Bitcoin first faces the 200-day EMA near $76,497, then some weak and immediate near $80,000. Friday's daily candle is still open, with its $74,780.91 low the immediate level to defend.
